body:
V3.2 Unintended Content Interpretation

> Rendering content or functionality in an incorrect context can lead to a wide variety of security issues.

can lead to malicious content execution?

---

V3.3 Cookie Setup

> This section provides requirements for how to securely configure sensitive cookies to reduce the risk of them being stolen or used inappropriately.


Something like (but those "and"-s needs some work):
> This section provides requirements for how to configure cookies to reduce the risk of being exposed to unintended sphere and to provide for the application confidence that the cookie is written by itself and it is not manipulated.


---

V3.4 Browser Security Mechanism Headers

> This section indicates which security headers should be set on HTTP responses to prevent various types of attack that could disclose sensitive data.

Input for further wordsmithing:
> This section provides requirements for HTTP response header fields configuration how the application can instruct the browser to enable security features and restrictions when handling the response from the application.

comments.body: Opened #2859 but I am open to other suggestions

3.2
> Rendering content or functionality in an incorrect context can lead to a malicious content being executed or shown.

It will be shown anyway. ("or shown" should be removed)

---

3.3

My proposal " for the application confidence that the cookie is written by itself and it is not manipulated." was to address the fact, that if a cookie with the same name but with a different domain or path value is written, then the application can not make the difference. `__Host-`, `__Secure-` and `Secure` is to provide confidence for the application on some parameters to be expected one.

Text from PR focuses only on modifying a existing cookie and does not address the main scoping problem.
> or being inappropriately modified.

---

3.4 - one extra space between browser and security

> 3.2
> 
> > Rendering content or functionality in an incorrect context can lead to a malicious content being executed or shown.
> 
> It will be shown anyway. ("or shown" should be removed)

I am thinking of a content injection where, for example an image gets rendered by HTML when it should just be text or something.

> 3.3
> 
> My proposal " for the application confidence that the cookie is written by itself and it is not manipulated." was to address the fact, that if a cookie with the same name but with a different domain or path value is written, then the application can not make the difference. `__Host-`, `__Secure-` and `Secure` is to provide confidence for the application on some parameters to be expected one.
> 
> Text from PR focuses only on modifying a existing cookie and does not address the main scoping problem.
>
> "_or being inappropriately modified_"

How about:

"_to be sure that it was created by the application itself and to avoid its contents leaking or being inappropriately modified._"

> 3.4 - one extra space between browser and security

Will fix

> "to be sure that it was created by the application itself and to avoid its contents leaking or being inappropriately modified."

The thing is that just by cookie parameters itself the application can not be sure, only when signing and checking the cookie value it can be sure. We can only talk about increased confidence. This is how the spec explains it as well https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-20#name-cookie-name-prefixes

> > "to be sure that it was created by the application itself and to avoid its contents leaking or being inappropriately modified."
> 
> The thing is that just by cookie parameters itself the application can not be sure, only when signing and checking the cookie value it can be sure. We can only talk about increased confidence. This is how the spec explains it as well https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-httpbis-rfc6265bis-20#name-cookie-name-prefixes

Ok so maybe:

"_to provide a higher level of assurance that it was created by the application itself and to avoid its contents leaking or being inappropriately modified._"
I update the wording based on last proposal.
